question: During which period were coal mines nationalised in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1971-1975**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The nationalization of coal mines in India occurred during the period **1971-1975**.
 
• The process began with the **nationalization of coking coal mines** through the Coking Coal Mines (Emergency Provisions) Act, 1971.
 
• In **1973**, the Coal Mines (Nationalization) Act was passed, extending nationalization to non-coking coal mines.
 
• The nationalization aimed to regulate coal production, improve safety measures, and ensure equitable distribution of coal resources.
 
• The nationalized coal mines were brought under the control of public sector companies like **Coal India Limited (CIL)** and its subsidiaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coal India Limited (CIL)**

 
 
• CIL is a public sector company established in **1975** and is headquartered in Kolkata, India.
 
• It is the largest coal-producing company in the world and operates under the Ministry of Coal.
 
• CIL is responsible for meeting the growing energy demands of India through coal production.
 
 
 
• **Types of Coal**
 
 
• Coal is classified into different types based on carbon content: **Anthracite, Bituminous, Sub-bituminous, and Lignite**.
 
• Coking coal is used in steel production, while non-coking coal is primarily used for electricity generation.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Nationalization**
 
 
• The coal industry faced challenges such as unscientific mining practices, poor safety standards, and exploitation of labor.
 
• Nationalization aimed to address these issues and ensure efficient use of coal resources for national development.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Nationalization**
 
 
• It led to the creation of a structured and organized coal industry in India.
 
• Nationalization improved safety measures, working conditions, and production efficiency.
 
• It enabled the government to control coal prices and ensure equitable distribution.
